page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. The server includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the average tier. Memory bandwidth is balanced, registering 1177.67 GB/sec for cached reads and 118.62 GB/sec for uncached reads. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-level AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution without the performance degradation associated with shared-core environments. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. However, memory-intensive operations or large-scale LLM inference represent a potential tradeoff, as demonstrated by the weaker prompt processing speeds on 7B parameter models.
This server is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
